features.name: v1_std_zone_bucket
features.description: Three-zone ordinal bucket for V1 using training-fold mean +/- one standard deviation: 0 below lower cut, 1 middle zone, 2 above upper cut.
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a direct low/mid/high split candidate so shallow trees can isolate extreme V1 regions without learning two separate numeric cuts.

features.name: v2_std_zone_bucket
features.description: Three-zone ordinal bucket for V2 using training-fold mean +/- one standard deviation: 0 below lower cut, 1 middle zone, 2 above upper cut.
features.expected_model_benefit: Supports early branching on high or low V2 regimes while preserving a simple middle-region grouping.

features.name: v3_std_zone_bucket
features.description: Three-zone ordinal bucket for V3 using training-fold mean +/- one standard deviation: 0 below lower cut, 1 middle zone, 2 above upper cut.
features.expected_model_benefit: Offers a compact V3 regime code that can be split directly and combined with other bucketed measurements.

features.name: v5_low_tail_indicator
features.description: Binary flag for V5 falling more than one training-fold standard deviation below its mean.
features.expected_model_benefit: Lets trees quickly separate rows with unusually depressed fifth measurement values.

features.name: v1_v2_joint_high_indicator
features.description: Binary interaction flag for simultaneous upper-zone values in V1 and V2 based on training-fold mean plus one standard deviation cuts.
features.expected_model_benefit: Captures co-occurrence in the first two measurements, reducing the depth needed for an equivalent pair of splits.

features.name: high_std_zone_count
features.description: Count of V1-V5 measurements that exceed their training-fold mean plus one standard deviation.
features.expected_model_benefit: Compresses multi-column upper-tail information into an ordinal feature with natural tree split points.

features.name: low_std_zone_count
features.description: Count of V1-V5 measurements that fall below their training-fold mean minus one standard deviation.
features.expected_model_benefit: Gives trees a simple ordinal measure of how broadly low-valued the row profile is across all five measurements.

features.name: front_back_contrast
features.description: Signed contrast between the first two measurements and the last two measurements.
features.expected_model_benefit: Highlights broad profile tilt, allowing direct splits on whether early positions dominate late positions or the reverse.

features.name: center_edge_contrast
features.description: Difference between V3 and the average of the two endpoint measurements V1 and V5.
features.expected_model_benefit: Exposes center-versus-edge structure that would otherwise require combining three raw measurements.

features.name: profile_roughness
features.description: Total adjacent absolute variation across the ordered five-measurement trace.
features.expected_model_benefit: Enables a single split to distinguish smooth profiles from jagged profiles with multiple sharp changes.
features.formula: np.abs(V2 - V1) + np.abs(V3 - V2) + np.abs(V4 - V3) + np.abs(V5 - V4)

features.name: qualitative_trace_shape_score
features.description: Ordinal evaluator score from the five-measurement trace only: 0 nearly flat, 1 mostly rising, 2 mostly falling, 3 one clear interior crest or trough, 4 multiple turns or irregular profile.
features.expected_model_benefit: Adds a compact semantic shape code that trees can branch on directly when numeric slopes express the pattern only across multiple variables.

features.name: qualitative_extreme_balance_score
features.description: Ordinal evaluator score from V1-V5 only: 0 extremes concentrated at V4-V5, 1 mildly concentrated at V4-V5, 2 balanced across positions, 3 mildly concentrated at V1-V2, 4 strongly concentrated at V1-V2.
features.expected_model_benefit: Supplies a semantic summary of where large magnitudes appear, giving trees an easy coarse grouping for profile balance.
